findings.issue: This bullet is in the Expansive Depth Mode section, and it says a lineage with no `--iters` runs 12 iterations. Under expansive depth that is wrong. fanout-run.cjs:339-351 (`expansiveLineageBudgets`) gives every lineage the matrix left without iterations its own count, using `expansiveBudget`. A review lineage dealt at least one seed node gets min(24, max(floor, 2*4*(share+2))), which is 24. A lineage dealt no seed node gets its loop default: 12 for a native lineage, and 7 (`LOOP_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS.review`) for a CLI one. The fallback `lineage.iterations || 12` (fanout-run.cjs:1858) is reached only when depth is not expansive. Line 238 of the same file states the derived behavior correctly.

fix.new: when unset, derived from the lineage's seed share up to 24, or its loop default of 12 native and 7 CLI when it was dealt no seed node

findings.issue: The doc says the seed step rewrites `maxIterations`. `step_frontier_seed` (deep-review.yaml:901-925) only runs `frontier-admit.cjs seed` and never writes the config. `step_frontier_budget` (deep-review.yaml:927-954) is the step that writes `maxIterations: budget.derivedMaxIterations` into deep-review-config.json. Row 38 of this same file names `step_frontier_budget` correctly.

fix.old: Under a defaulted budget the seed step rewrites `maxIterations` itself
fix.new: Under a defaulted budget `step_frontier_budget` rewrites `maxIterations` itself

findings.issue: The fan-out sizing rule says a lineage node's universe is 'the four canonical dimensions plus every configured custom name'. fanout-run.cjs hard-codes `review_dimensions: all` in every review lineage's setup bindings (lines 1793 and 1892). A lineage config therefore never holds a custom name, so a lineage node's universe is the canonical four only. `expansiveLineageBudgets` (fanout-run.cjs:337-348) also sizes a lineage with D fixed at 4. The doc should say that fan-out lineages review the canonical four and ignore configured custom dimensions, and that the sizing rule uses those four.

The Next Focus precedence puts the leaf's nextFocus unconditionally ahead of the first uncovered dimension. In runtime/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2397-2405 (`pickReviewBaseFocus`), the leaf focus is used only when it names an uncovered dimension or every dimension is already covered. Otherwise the first uncovered dimension wins over the leaf focus. SKILL.md:241 carries the same simplified order.
